data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Chemical agents, peels & baths_

**Class:** Bath additives used as adjunct therapy

## Mechanism of action
- Hydrate and soften scale, remove crusts and exudate, reduce bacterial load, soothe itch; allow treatment of large body surfaces

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Colloidal oatmeal bath: itch of atopic dermatitis, varicella, urticaria (anti-inflammatory avenanthramides)
- Oil baths (emollient bath oils): xerosis, ichthyosis, atopic dermatitis (slippery — fall risk)
- Potassium permanganate bath (1:10,000): weeping/infected eczema, pemphigus, bullous disorders
- Dilute bleach baths: atopic dermatitis with recurrent staphylococcal infections
- Tar baths (Ingram regimen), bath PUVA (trioxsalen/8-MOP), salt (Dead Sea) baths for psoriasis
- Cleansing baths for erosive and blistering diseases; wax bath (paraffin) for joint stiffness in scleroderma hands

## Dose & formulations
- 10–15 min, lukewarm water, followed by emollient within 3 min (soak and seal)

## Adverse effects
- Over-drying with prolonged hot baths; KMnO₄ staining/burns; slipping in oil baths

## Contraindications
- Hot baths in rosacea/urticaria flares (heat aggravates)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Soak-and-seal; KMnO₄ 1:10,000; bleach bath in AD; Ingram regimen tar baths

_Sources: Khopkar ch.33 (Baths — cleansing, oatmeal, oil, potassium permanganate, wax bath). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
